processing: Black tea of pure orthodox manufacture: withered, rolled, fully oxidised and fired.
harvest_season: Picked through the year; lots from the Uva quality season are the prized ones.
appearance_dry: Typical of orthodox Uva grades: dark, wiry leaf, sized by grade such as OP.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish amber, on the delicate side for a black tea.
appearance_wet: Coppery brown open leaf, as with other orthodox Ceylon teas.
taste_profile: Known for delicate liquoring, especially in the Uva quality season; expect the brisk, clean character typical of Uva rather than heavy malt.

brewing.notes: Western-style. A delicate lot loses its charm under milk, so try the first cup plain.

vintage_note: Sold by grade through the Colombo auction, in the Uva Medium category, with quality-season invoices commanding the higher prices. As usual for Ceylon black tea, buy recent manufacture and drink within a year or two.
description:
Adawatte is an estate near Lunugala in Uva Province, making orthodox black tea. It is a mid-elevation Uva garden, sold in the Uva Medium auction category, which is a useful thing to know before comparing it with the taller estates around Haputale.

The tea is pure orthodox, meaning rolled leaf rather than CTC granules. That usually gives a more delicate, layered cup, and delicacy is exactly what the estate is known for during the Uva quality season.

Brew it Western-style, with water just off the boil, for three to four minutes. Try it plain first; the character that makes it worth seeking is easily buried by milk.

When buying, the season matters more than the name. Ask whether the lot is from the quality season, and treat a seller who only says Ceylon or Uva with some caution.
history:
Sources disagree on the start date: 1904 is the year most often given, while one trade blog says 1938 and adds that the factory was rebuilt in 1956. An estate register also lists records from 1904 to 1925.

Ownership has moved over time. It was described as under Finlays in 2009, and in 2022 as part of Hapugastenne Plantations, managed by Browns Plantations. That September an OP grade reached Rs. 2,250 per kg, an all-time record for the estate.
